compiled_state.author: Rebar Bot
compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

CLI users need to see the cross-session warning inline. rebar already has a stderr
`WARN:`/`WARNING:` convention that leaves stdout and exit codes untouched
(`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:99` `warn_secret_screen_refused`; the fsck `WARN:` lines in
`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py`). This story emits that warning for CLI commands that
target **one specific ticket**, and — per the brainstorm scope — **never** for bulk reads
(`list` / `search` / `ready` / `next-batch`).

Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, sibling story) and on the reducer
clearing (so a non-`in_progress` ticket has no holder and never warns).

## Approach

Define the single-ticket-targeted CLI command set as an **explicit, data-driven
allowlist** (a frozenset in the CLI dispatch layer) rather than inferring it, so bulk-read
commands are excluded by construction. The set covers single-ticket reads and mutations:
`show`, `comment`, `edit`, `transition`, `reopen`, `tag`, `untag`, `set-file-impact`,
`declare-no-file-impact`, `deps`, `archive`, `check-ac`, `clarity-check`, `link`,
`unlink`. It excludes `list`, `search`, `ready`, `next-batch`, and `create` (no
pre-existing target). For `link` / `unlink` (two endpoints) the warning is computed for the
**primary** ticket argument (`id1`) only.

At the point where a single-ticket CLI command has resolved its ticket id (the shared
`require_id` seam, `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:157`, and the id resolution the read arms
use), call `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, tracker=..., repo_root=...)`; when it
returns a string, `sys.stderr.write("WARN: " + msg + "\n")` **before** performing the
operation, so the warning is visible even if the op itself is quiet. stdout content and the
process exit code are unchanged. `claim` is intentionally **not** in the set: claiming an
`in_progress` ticket already fails with `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10 before any warning path
(`docs/concurrency.md`).

The warning is computed from the ticket state **at operation time** (before a mutation
applies), so e.g. a `transition <id> in_progress closed` run by another session warns about
holder A and *then* clears the provenance — the read precedes the write.

## Scope

- The CLI dispatch / single-ticket id-resolution seam under `src/rebar/_cli/` and/or
  `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (`require_id`) — add the allowlist + the stderr emit at the
  resolved-id point. Confirm the exact insertion seam by reading the dispatch during
  implementation; the allowlist is the single source of "which commands warn".
- `docs/user-guide.md` — a short note that single-ticket CLI commands warn on stderr when
  another session holds the ticket, and that bulk commands do not.

## Testing

Tier: **real CLI subprocess + persisted-state assertion** (test-design §3 "CLI parsing,
streams, env, exit codes" — the mechanism crosses argv parsing, env-var session resolution,
and stderr). Use a real temporary tracker; set `REBAR_SESSION_ID` per invocation to model
distinct sessions.

- Claim a ticket with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=A` (so `claimed_session=A`). Run `rebar show <id>`
  and `rebar comment <id> "x"` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=B`: assert **stderr** contains `WARN:`
  and the holder id `A`, stdout is the normal output, and exit code is `0`.
- Negative control (same session): the same commands with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=A` emit **no**
  `WARN:` line (exit 0).
- Bulk exclusion: `rebar list` (and `rebar ready`) with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=B` emit **no**
  `WARN:` line even though the store contains A's `in_progress` ticket.
- Unset-id silence: `rebar show <id>` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset emits no `WARN:` line.
- Defect-seeded: temporarily point the emit at the wrong ticket / drop the allowlist guard
  and show the bulk-exclusion and holder-id assertions go RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With ticket held by session A, `rebar show <id>` and `rebar comment <id> ...` run as
  session B print a `WARN:` line naming holder `A` to **stderr**, with unchanged stdout and
  exit code 0 (checked by a CLI subprocess test under `make test`).
- [ ] Negative control: the same commands as session A print no `WARN:` line (checked by the
  same test asserting stderr has no `WARN:`).
- [ ] `rebar list` and `rebar ready` as session B print no cross-session `WARN:` line even
  with A's `in_progress` ticket present (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [ ] `rebar show <id>` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset prints no `WARN:` line (checked by an
  unset-id assertion).
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents the CLI stderr warning and the bulk exclusion (checked:
  `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` matches).
